---
title: "Using the spreadsheet"
guide-section: "Spreadsheet Guide"
---

Use this guide when you want to run the official LIC-DSF spreadsheet directly,
without using the Python package. The workbook remains the economist-facing
tool: enter country assumptions on Inputs 1–8, review its checks, and interpret
the resulting debt paths and risk signals.

## Download the workbook

[Download the official macro-enabled LIC-DSF template](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/f0ade6bcf85b6f98dbeb2c39a2b7770c-0360012025/original/LIC-DSF-IDA21-Template-08-12-2025-vf.xlsm){.btn .btn-primary}

This guide covers the **August 12, 2025 IDA21 vintage**. Keep the file as
`.xlsm`, open it in a desktop version of Microsoft Excel, and enable its
content only after confirming that it came from the official World Bank link
above. Other spreadsheet applications may not reproduce its formulas, charts,
or VBA behavior.

The expected SHA-256 checksum is:

```text
3a0a0b80c7cbc95ac953f25ecae0b437129d669ceb8aeefb54ab86dc8727ea86
```

The workbook is a joint IMF/World Bank work and is not covered by this
package's software license. Follow the terms of the official source when
redistributing it.

## Recommended workflow

1. Save a country-specific copy; do not work in your clean template.
2. Read `Input-INSTRUCTIONS` and complete the yellow cells on Inputs 1–8.
3. Preserve sheet names, formulas, named ranges, and workbook structure.
4. Resolve the workbook's validation messages before interpreting results.
5. Review baseline debt dynamics before stress tests and ratings.
6. Use Realism and Probability outputs as evidence for economist judgement;
   they do not automatically replace the mechanical rating.
7. Record data vintages, coverage choices, overrides, and judgement separately.

## Input reference

The [spreadsheet input guide](09-spreadsheet-inputs.qmd) maps the
published calculation inputs to their workbook cells and ranges. It is
generated from `inputs.bindings.yaml`, including:

- country, vintage, discount-rate, and debt-coverage settings;
- macroeconomic and debt history/projections;
- external and domestic financing assumptions;
- standardized and tailored stress settings;
- residual financing, SDR, and customized-scenario inputs.

The binding reference is a cell map, not economic guidance. Units, sign
conventions, required vintages, and applicability still follow the workbook's
instructions and the IMF/World Bank LIC-DSF guidance.

## Output reference

The [spreadsheet output guide](10-spreadsheet-outputs.qmd) maps the
published `Chart Data` results to their workbook cells and ranges. It covers:

- external, fiscal, and overall mechanical risk signals;
- baseline and stress breach flags;
- most-extreme-shock labels;
- tailored-stress applicability;
- moderate-risk fiscal-space text;
- scenario-by-year paths used by the standard debt-stress figures.

The output bindings do not represent every formatted cell on Outputs 1–7.
Realism diagnostics, probability results, judgement, chart chrome, and VBA are
separate workbook surfaces.
